original_question: Does there exist a geproci set in linearly general position, or can one prove that no linearly general geproci set exists?
target_in_paper: The draft does not match arXiv:2311.03081, whose title is "List of Problems" and whose topic is Lefschetz properties. The nearest paper-faithful target matching the draft is the geproci open problem recalled in Section 1 of arXiv:2407.01744 from [4, Question 0.2]: whether geproci sets in ℙ^3 in linear general position exist apart from four general points.
correct_elements: The draft correctly identifies the core issue: the existence versus nonexistence of geproci sets in linear general position. It also captures that the intended problem is an open classification/existence question, not a request for a construction of a specific known example.
missing_details: The ambient space is missing: the paper's question is about finite sets of points in projective 3-space, Z ⊂ ℙ^3.
The ground field is missing: the paper works over the complex numbers.

The object 'geproci set' must be defined: one asks for a finite reduced set of points Z such that projection from a general point of ℙ^3 to a plane is a complete intersection; in Definition 2.1 this is stated more precisely as an (a,b)-geproci set whose general projection is the transverse intersection of plane curves of degrees a and b.
The draft omits the paper-critical exception 'apart from four general points'; without this, the question is false as stated because four general points are the basic known LGP example.
The draft does not specify whether the question is about some pair (a,b) or about geproci sets in general; the paper's open problem is existential over all possible (a,b), not for a fixed pair.
The phrase 'linearly general position' should be made stand-alone; in ℙ^3 this means, in standard usage, that no four points are coplanar.
The quantifier should be explicit: one asks whether there exists any finite reduced geproci set in LGP other than four general points, or equivalently whether none exist beyond that trivial case.
The scope should be kept narrow: this is about geproci sets in ℙ^3, not geprofi sets in higher-dimensional projective spaces, and not about grids/half-grids or positive-characteristic variants.
refined_question: Over ℚ, does there exist a finite reduced set of points Z ⊂ ℙ^3 in linear general position (i.e. no four points coplanar), other than a set of four general points, for which there exist integers a ≤ b such that the projection of Z from a general point of ℙ^3 to ℙ^2 is the transverse complete intersection of two plane curves of degrees a and b?
justification: The supplied arXiv identifier 2311.03081 is unrelated to geproci sets, so the draft cannot be matched inside that paper. The draft instead matches the geproci LGP open problem recalled in the introduction of arXiv:2407.01744, which explicitly says that [4, Question 0.2] asks about the existence of geproci sets in ℙ^3 in linear general position apart from four general points, and that this question remains open. Definition 2.1 in the same paper supplies the precise geproci terminology needed to make the question self-contained. Section 5 repeats the same conjectural nonexistence statement for geproci sets in LGP, confirming that this is the exact nearby problem your draft is aiming at rather than a broader neighboring question.
